items.review_rationale: Read the finite spanning-list criterion and equivalent surjection from a finite free module, preserving the module rather than algebra context and identifying ordinary linear surjectivity.

references.context: Direct sum of n copies of R as a left R-module, with canonical standard basis
Every m∈M is the image of some n-tuple of coefficients from R
Set of finite sums Σ r_i m_i with coefficients r_i∈R, required to equal M

references.phrase: equivalence of generating list and finite free surjection
references.disposition: An equivalent criterion for finite generation, not an extra injectivity or projectivity condition.

items.review_rationale: Read the finite presentation of an R-module as an exact sequence between finite-rank free modules and M, including the finite relation module and image-kernel exactness; not confused with finite presentation of a ring algebra.

references.phrase: finite free modules R^m and R^n
references.context: Finite direct sums of copies of R in the sequence, not arbitrary finitely generated projective modules
Finite list generating the kernel of the surjection R^n→M, expressed by the image of R^m

references.disposition: Both generators and relations are finite; finite generation of M alone is insufficient over a non-Noetherian ring.

items.review_rationale: Read the additive order of 1_F and zero-characteristic alternative in a field, including integer scalar multiples and the consequence that positive characteristic is prime.

references.context: Sum of n copies of the multiplicative identity of F in its additive group
Additive order of 1_F if finite, with zero characteristic defined if no positive such n exists
Positive integer greater than 1 divisible only by 1 and itself, not a prime ideal of a ring

references.disposition: An algebraic theorem following from field axioms, not an additional independent part of the definition.

items.review_rationale: Read uniqueness and minimality of the prime subfield of F, distinguishing the Q case of characteristic zero and the F_p case of positive prime characteristic; checked that a subfield is an embedded field, not an abstract isomorphic copy alone.

references.context: Subset containing the field identities and closed under addition, multiplication, additive inverses and inversion of nonzero elements

references.phrase: smallest subfield of F by inclusion
references.context: Intersection of all subfields of F, or subfield generated by 1_F, compared under inclusion
Unital bijective homomorphism of fields respecting the stated characteristic, not literal equality of underlying sets

references.phrase: Q when char 0 and F_p when char p>0
references.disposition: The characteristic-dependent identification is the standard structural classification, not two simultaneously contained prime subfields.
